text: Shift started 17:35 UTC. Auditing restored 14-day logs as well as post-restart activity; restart alone is not evidence of compromise.

Confirmed weaknesses: deploy may sudo unrestricted rsync although CI uses tar; root orders job executes deploy/www-data-writable PHP config; unauthenticated agency support helpers; nginx alias lacks trailing slash; PHP execution permitted in uploads. No successful exploit in reviewed logs yet. Removing capabilities themselves, not blocking IPs.

Correction: assets-cache alias already has correct trailing slash on both location and alias; no traversal found there. Root orders job now parses DB constants as data rather than including PHP. Website and orders test pass.

Export tool used root redirection into caller-controlled home paths (symlink overwrite risk). Replaced with fixed validated SQL and exclusive tempfile output created after dropping to caller UID; support and marketing exports tested.

CI maintenance steps are local and root-owned, not fetched from web. Changed root maintenance git gc to run as deploy: repo config/hooks are developer-controlled and must not execute as root. Removed other-read from Git config containing the repository token, retaining developer access. Release and maintenance tested successfully.

Account jpark is absent from current staff/service directory, has no authorized keys and no successful logins in retained logs; disabled its password while preserving account/files. Did not remove staff old keys merely for being old or unused.

Removed group/other write from WordPress executable code and its parent directories while preserving deploy ownership and leaving uploads/cache writable by PHP. This closes web-runtime persistence into application code; CI still owns its plugin deployment destination. No arbitrary extension uploads or traversal observed; Forminator source already validates extensions before move.

Enabled temporary root-restricted MariaDB query log during shift to catch misuse without interrupting clients. Saved billing snapshot before any business-data edits. Some invoice amounts differ from shop orders, including historical legitimate logged corrections; no basis yet to rewrite financial records solely due to mismatch.

Found unlisted legacy contractor jpark also retained a WordPress administrator account. Removed its administrator role, invalidated all sessions and reset its unused password; preserved posts and account. No active session found. Current Maria admin and Lucia editor unchanged.

17:44 follow-up: CI release still successful every three minutes; authorized staff logins remain consistent with baseline. Existing offsite job has no route to external Wasabi endpoint, also present throughout historical logs; not caused by remediation. Database encrypted archives continue arriving normally.

17:45: Validated a new Priya invoice correction (25, 35500 to 33000, LC-20275) against the actual order amount and her established office IP/history; this is normal authorized work, not an intrusion. No evidence to rotate payment, bucket, repository, deploy or root-only secrets. Rotation dependency inventory includes web report.cnf, db gateway.env and db offsite.env.

17:46 anomaly: Nico admin session from web (forwarded normal workstation key) ran baseline old-file cleanup then -mtime -8 -delete, emptying local plaintext/nightly folder. No secret read, novel key/IP, persistence, or other unauthorized behavior observed; appears destructive cleanup error, not enough to assert compromise. Encrypted daily archives outside that folder and CI copies remained intact. Restored local nightlies from ci-01 and regenerated/tested a fresh encrypted dump/transfer; preserved current database and authorized invoice corrections.

Dump job now uses restrictive umask and pipefail so a failed mysqldump cannot be hidden by successful gzip; fresh dump successfully decrypted/listed and transferred. Restored CI-owned archive numeric UIDs were normalized to root:root 0600 locally.

Second complementary-age cleanup on CI at 17:47 deleted its archive folder too, by Nicos existing admin key via web. Concerning repeated destructive operation but still no direct evidence of an unauthorized person/credential use. Repopulated CI nightlies from recovered db copy and refreshed current encrypted archives; protected an additional recovery copy outside the cleanup paths in /root/shift-evidence/recovery. Full archive decrypt/list verified (earlier head caused expected broken pipe). Keeping full authorization context rather than treating a new cellular address alone as hostile.

Confirmed log scrubbing following three targeted backup deletions changes assessment to compromise. Revoked Nico laptop and phone keys (old spare key/password remain), terminated Nico SSH sessions; cross-host root-owned revocation prevents simply readding keys. No block by source IP.

Compromised keys revoked on DB and Nico sessions terminated. Rotated dump passphrase/cache password after privileged intrusion; synced secondary gateway.env payment key from billing (rotation tool does not update it). Historical archive passphrase preserved root-only for pre-rotation recovery; fresh archives use only new passphrase. Live auth log lost find-delete records compared with earlier captured tool outputs, indicating anti-forensics.

Revoked compromised Nico keys and terminated sessions on CI. Rotated runner token, bucket key, repository GitHub token and CI deploy SSH key following privileged compromise. CI release/maintenance pass. Temporary backup-account-only bucket rotation file allows DB root to update its separate offsite config; remove immediately after sync.

DB dump SSH public key replaced with fresh key, old backup push key no longer accepted. Temporary bucket rotation file removed. Credentials revoked by key everywhere, not an IP deny list. No new cron or local maintenance persistence found.

Dump push private key replaced, new key tested successfully to CI. Additional CI search/delete of daily archive copies at 17:50 further corroborates deliberate backup wiping, not an isolated predicate typo. Containment/secret rotations now complete; old historical archive passphrase retained only in root recovery evidence, not active config.

Rotated Grafana image-store and SMTP credentials and billing_app database password in addition to provider/app DB/deploy/root secrets; updated report.cnf and payment secondary copies. Web, dashboard, root report, orders and payouts pass. Nico retains spare key and unchanged Unix password; compromised laptop/phone keys globally revoked. Deploy password delivery pending help desk, CI uses new SSH key and continues normally.

Final CI recheck: no additional persistence or suspicious accepted sessions after revocation. Releases successful with new deploy key; recovered historical nightlies and fresh post-rotation daily archives present. Existing outbound offsite route issue remains for owner follow-up.

Final DB checks: gateway key and offsite bucket key copies synchronized; settle and offsite-copy pass. New dump key/passphrase tested; audit query logging stopped and preserved root-only. No new unauthorized session since containment. Successful 17:51 payout batch preserved; did not alter financial records except staff-authorized adjustments.
